message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations you should know: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are mandatory; no “reasonable speed” exception.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (varies by county).
• In school zones: 25 mph during school hours unless posted otherwise. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine plus points. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time.
• First offense: up to 90 days jail, $500 fine, 2‑point penalty. | | **Traffic Signal & Stop‑Sign Rules** | • Must come to a complete stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the main road have priority.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 12 months leads to a 30‑day license suspension.
• 6 points in 24 months results in a 90‑day suspension. | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | • Annual vehicle inspection required (except exempt categories).
• Registration renewal due annually; late fees apply. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 25 mph during school hours (or as posted).
• Violations can incur a $100 fine and 2 points. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists must ride in the lane if one exists; otherwise, they may use the shoulder.
• Motorcycles must display a license plate on both front and rear. | ### Quick Tips for Compliance 1. **Always obey posted signs** – Texas law does not allow “reasonable speed” exceptions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on your phone. 3. **Check your points** – you can view your current status online via the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) website. 4. **Keep your registration and inspection stickers up to date** – failure to do so can result in a $200 fine. If you’re looking for more detailed statutes or specific case law, let me know!
